companies.latest_signal: CEO Xu Ran called Q2 2026 a 'clear inflection point' in profitability, with management saying total delivery investment fell over 50% yoy as commission/ad monetization from JD Takeaway roughly doubled and per-order economics kept improving.

war_summary: Subsidy intensity peaked around Q3 2025 (combined Meituan+Alibaba daily orders near 180m, an estimated RMB150bn+ burned across the three in under a year) before regulatory pressure under Beijing's 'anti-involution' campaign and investor pushback forced a coordinated pullback into 2026. By Q2 2026 all three show narrowing losses on their own disclosed proxies — Meituan's core local commerce flipped back to profit fastest, JD's new-business loss is down over 50% yoy, and Alibaba's EBITA drag is easing yoy though still large in absolute terms. Meituan has blinked least (still ~65m daily orders, largest share), Alibaba is committed longest (internal 3-year no-loss mandate on Flash Sale, breakeven not guided until FY2029), and JD — with the smallest order base (~9m/day) — has throttled spending fastest.
